question: Before implementing the frozen C10.65b rank solve, is its simultaneous use of ordinary inter-species adiabaticity and the absolute neutral zero-charge condition I_khr=0 mutually compatible on the nonzero-curvature baseline growing branch?

definitions.preferred_invariance: delta_i,pref/(1+w_i)=delta_i,N/(1+w_i)+3 H B and Psi_N=psi_pref-HB imply J_i=delta_i,pref/(1+w_i)-3 psi_pref

evaluation.fit: independent least-squares affine fits J_i(x)=J_i0+s_i x for b,g,ur using the three smallest positive k values from C10.65a

preregistered_tolerances.note: The compatibility threshold is orders of magnitude above the C10.65a density-control floor and is fixed before this script evaluates the parent records.

classification_rule.C10_65B0_ZERO_CHARGE_ADIABATIC_COMPATIBL: ordinary intercepts are common within 1e-6 and |J_ad0|<=1e-4
classification_rule.C10_65B0_ZERO_CHARGE_ADIABATIC_INCOMPATI: ordinary intercepts are common within 1e-6 and |J_ad0|>1e-4, so J_khr=0 carries nonzero relative entropy on the ordinary growing branch
classification_rule.C10_65B0_PREFLIGHT_TECHNICAL_AMBIGUOUS: ordinary low-k intercepts fail the common-intercept guard or required parent data are nonfinite

architecture_if_incompatible.do_not_execute_as_written: Do not interpret the frozen C10.65b zero-charge system as an adiabatic rank theorem.
architecture_if_incompatible.replacement_adiabatic_boundary: I_khr(tau_on)=J_ad(tau_on), equivalently delta_khr/(1+w_khr)-3 psi_pref=J_ad, where J_ad is the common ordinary curvature/entropy invariant in the same normalization.
architecture_if_incompatible.isocurvature_coordinate: Delta I_iso=I_khr-J_ad; the adiabatic branch sets Delta I_iso=0, while nonzero Delta I_iso remains the independent neutral charge-isocurvature sector.
architecture_if_incompatible.C10_64_status: Retain the exact C10.64 zero-charge theorem as a valid charge-sector boundary theorem, but supersede its labeling as the generic nonzero-curvature adiabatic branch if this preflight is incompatible.
